newsitem.title: UK: Aluminium smelting capacity to jump in July-Dec.
newsitem.headline: Aluminium smelting capacity to jump in July-Dec.

text.p: Substantial growth in aluminium smelting capacity is due later this year and may pressure prices if demand dips at the same time, broker Brandeis said in a report.
The second half of 1997 is expected to see an increase of 482,000 tonnes in primary capacity, it said.
"New production capacity due on stream later this year, which if it coincides with slower demand growth, could exert downwards pressure on prices," the report said.
"Many of the expansion programmes at existing smelters are being completed ahead of schedule and this accounts for the large increase in production capacity during second half 1997," it added.
Scheduled capacity increases were estimated at 124,000 tonnes in the first half of 1997, 482,000 in the second half, 192,000 for the first half of 1998 and 90,000 tonnes in the second half of 1998.
The global economy should remain favourable through 1998, and Western aluminium consumption should grow by 3.5 percent in both 1997 and 1998.

"Our main concern is centred on demand and the fact that this was boosted by consumer restocking over the first five months of this year and as a result, is unlikely to be repeated in second half 1997," the report said.
